question: What is retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and who introduced the term?
expected_points: combines a retriever with a generator; external documents are added to the model context; introduced by Lewis et al. (2020, Facebook AI)

question: What is the ReAct prompting framework for LLM agents?
expected_points: interleaves reasoning traces and actions; observations from tools feed the next step; Yao et al. 2022

question: What is the transformer architecture and which paper introduced it?
expected_points: based on self-attention without recurrence; 'Attention Is All You Need'; Vaswani et al. 2017

question: What is the Model Context Protocol (MCP)?
expected_points: open protocol introduced by Anthropic in 2024; standard way to connect LLM apps to tools and data sources; client-server design

question: What is the GAIA benchmark and what does it measure?
expected_points: benchmark for general AI assistants; real-world questions needing web browsing, tool use and reasoning; easy for humans, hard for models

question: What is Reflexion in LLM agents?
expected_points: agent writes verbal self-reflection after failure; reflection stored in memory for next attempt; no weight updates; Shinn et al. 2023

question: What is the context window of a large language model and why does it matter?
expected_points: maximum number of tokens the model can process at once; limits how much retrieved text fits; long inputs raise cost and latency

question: What is the EU AI Act and when did it enter into force?
expected_points: EU regulation on AI with risk-based categories; entered into force August 2024; obligations phase in over several years

question: What is Toolformer and how does it learn to use tools?
expected_points: Meta AI 2023 (Schick et al.); model annotates its own training data with API calls; keeps calls that reduce loss; self-supervised

question: What is chain-of-thought prompting and in which paper was it proposed?
expected_points: prompting model to write intermediate reasoning steps; improves multi-step reasoning in large models; Wei et al. 2022

question: Compare ReAct and plan-and-execute agent designs.
expected_points: ReAct plans one step at a time; plan-and-execute writes a full plan first; plan-and-execute uses fewer LLM calls; ReAct adapts better to surprises

question: Compare dense and sparse (BM25) retrieval for RAG.
expected_points: BM25 matches exact keywords; dense uses embeddings and captures meaning; dense needs training/embedding model; hybrid often best

question: Compare fine-tuning and RAG for adding domain knowledge to an LLM.
expected_points: RAG updates knowledge without retraining and can cite sources; fine-tuning changes style/behaviour; fine-tuning is costly to refresh; RAG depends on retrieval quality

question: What are the differences between open-weight and closed LLMs for research use?
expected_points: open weights can be run locally and inspected; closed models are often stronger and easier via API; privacy and cost trade-offs; reproducibility

question: Compare single-agent and multi-agent LLM systems for complex tasks.
expected_points: multi-agent splits roles and can work in parallel; higher token cost and coordination overhead; single-agent simpler to debug; benefit depends on task

question: Compare vector databases such as FAISS, Chroma and Pinecone.
expected_points: FAISS is a library for similarity search; Chroma is open-source and easy local setup; Pinecone is a managed cloud service; trade-offs in scale, cost, hosting

question: Compare automatic metrics (BLEU, ROUGE) with LLM-as-a-judge for evaluating generated text.
expected_points: BLEU/ROUGE measure n-gram overlap and are cheap; weak correlation with quality for open-ended text; LLM judges correlate better with humans; LLM judges have biases (position, verbosity, self-preference)

question: How do web search APIs for LLM agents (e.g. Tavily, Bing, SerpAPI) differ?
expected_points: Tavily built for LLM agents and returns cleaned content; Bing/Google-style APIs return links and snippets; differences in price, freshness and limits

question: Compare prompt engineering, few-shot learning and instruction tuning.
expected_points: prompt engineering changes only input; few-shot puts examples in the prompt; instruction tuning updates weights on instruction data; cost and flexibility trade-offs

question: Compare OpenAI Deep Research, Gemini Deep Research and open-source research agents like GPT Researcher.
expected_points: all run multi-step search and write long reports; commercial tools are closed and paid; open-source can be self-hosted and changed; quality and citation accuracy vary

question: What are the main limitations of retrieval-augmented generation?
expected_points: quality depends on retrieval; irrelevant or conflicting passages; context length limits; model may still ignore or misread sources

question: Why do LLMs hallucinate citations and how can this be reduced?
expected_points: model generates plausible but non-existent references; reduce via retrieval grounding; verify citations against sources; quote passages

question: How can research agents defend against prompt injection from web pages?
expected_points: web text may contain hidden instructions; treat tool output as untrusted data; restrict tools and permissions; no full solution exists

question: What are the risks of using LLM agents for academic literature reviews?
expected_points: missed or hallucinated papers; bias toward easily accessible sources; shallow synthesis; need for human verification

question: Do larger language models always perform better? What is known about scaling limits?
expected_points: scaling laws show predictable loss decrease; diminishing returns; data limits; smaller models with better data/training can compete

question: What are the environmental costs of training and running large language models?
expected_points: high electricity use for training; inference at scale adds ongoing cost; water use for cooling; estimates vary and are disputed

question: Is LLM-as-a-judge evaluation reliable?
expected_points: agrees with humans in many settings; position and verbosity bias; self-preference bias; less reliable for expert domains

question: What copyright issues arise from training LLMs on web data?
expected_points: training on copyrighted text without permission; lawsuits by authors and publishers (e.g. NYT v. OpenAI); fair use debate; legal status still unsettled

question: How well do current LLM agents perform on long, multi-step tasks?
expected_points: success drops as task length grows; errors compound across steps; benchmarks like GAIA/WebArena show gap to humans; improving quickly

question: What are the privacy risks of sending user documents to LLM APIs?
expected_points: data leaves the user's control; possible retention or logging by provider; sensitive data must be removed; local models as alternative
